project.name: agent-agnostic-sync-orchestrator
project.description: AI Booster Kit is a modular, human-centred platform for choosing, tuning, validating, and reusing Agent or Multi-Agent capabilities without making Agent assistance mandatory. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

layers.name: Documentation and Contracts
layers.description: Roadmaps, contracts, runbooks, research, templates, and operating documents that define the agent-agnostic sync orchestrator.

layers.name: Application and Readiness
layers.description: Controller, domain, lifecycle, orchestration, planning, readiness, and event modules that implement bounded coordination.

layers.name: Integration and Evidence
layers.description: Host adapters, Jira/GitHub/Confluence connectors, and evidence boundaries that mediate external-system reads and read-back.

layers.name: Tests and Conformance
layers.description: Automated tests and fixtures that validate contracts, readiness decisions, host behavior, connectors, and controller flows.

layers.name: Tooling and Delivery
layers.description: CLI scripts, CI pipelines, and developer tools that build, validate, and deliver the repository.

layers.name: Website Surface
layers.description: The website application, worker, database schema, and browser-facing runtime surface.

layers.name: Configuration
layers.description: Project manifests, compiler/build settings, ignore rules, and other repository-level configuration.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the repository README to understand the agent-agnostic sync orchestrator and its operating boundary. It provides the vocabulary for the contract, readiness, connector, and delivery areas covered by the rest of the tour.

tour.title: Current Delivery Contract
tour.description: The current-state, roadmap, and mapper runbook explain what is actually ready, what remains stopped, and how source truth relates to generated navigation graphs. This is the project-level frame for interpreting the implementation without promoting historical or generated evidence.

tour.title: CLI and Request Flow
tour.description: The CLI and request/controller entry points turn an incoming task into a bounded decision flow. The formation recipe and request types connect user intent to the recommendation and readiness machinery implemented deeper in the application.

tour.title: Readiness Boundaries
tour.description: The readiness evaluator, run path, lifecycle start-check, and explicit stop handling define when work can proceed and when the system must fail closed. Together they make the READY, NOT READY, and STOPPED distinctions executable rather than merely descriptive.

tour.title: Integration and Evidence
tour.description: Adapters and Jira/GitHub/Confluence connectors form the external boundary, while evidence ingestion and read-back preserve provenance and independent verification. This layer is where authority, target identity, and native evidence are kept separate from local recommendations.

tour.title: Agent Recipes and Contracts
tour.description: The agent-library documents and formation recommendation code describe bounded scenarios such as debugging and the contract needed before a recommendation becomes actionable. They provide the human-readable operating projection over the typed controller behavior.

tour.title: Tests and Conformance
tour.description: Controller, readiness, debugging-recipe, and host-conformance tests show how the project checks both positive behavior and fail-closed boundaries. These tests are the executable evidence that connects the contracts to the implementation.

tour.title: Delivery Surface
tour.description: The package manifest, CI workflow, and website surface show how the repository is built, checked, and exposed to a user-facing runtime. This closes the tour by connecting local implementation and evidence rules to the delivery pipeline.
